name: Beat Lab
description: Diagnostic view of the beat tracker for judging it on your own music: the raw estimate (beat pulse, phase hand, BPM, confidence) next to the stable published clock shaders see (green hand, BPM, trust), kick flashes, band meters and a scrolling kicks-vs-beat-grid timeline.

data.text:
# Beat Lab
A diagnostic view for judging the beat tracker on your own music. Open the audio menu -> Mic (or File / Tab), play a track and watch. White = the tracker's raw (live) estimate (u_beatRaw, Beat node clock = raw); green = the stable published clock every other shader sees (u_beatPhase, u_bpm), which coasts while the estimate is untrusted and glides to a new tempo.
## Top left - the beat
- Circle flashes on each detected beat (orange = downbeat of the 4-beat bar, blue = other beats); dim = low confidence.
- The white hand sweeps once per beat (raw); the green dot outside the ring is the stable clock. They overlap when locked; after a track change the white hand jumps to the new beat while the green one keeps going, then glides onto it.
- The orange tick at 12 o'clock is where the beat lands.
- The 4 dots show the beat within the bar.
## Kick (middle)
- Flashes on detected kick onsets. If the tracker is right, kick and beat circle flash together.
## Right
- Raw BPM (large, bright when locked), stable BPM (small, green), thin green trust bar (u_beatTrust: 0 while the stable clock coasts), confidence bar (u_beatConfidence: green locked / amber tentative / red lost), level - bass - mid - high meters.
## Timeline (bottom, ~8 s, newest on the right)
- Orange spikes = kicks, blue = bass, white lines = raw beat grid (warm = downbeat), green ticks at the bottom = stable beats, top strip = confidence, bottom green strip = trust.
- Good tracking: white lines sit on the orange spikes and stay evenly spaced.
## If it's off
- Late/early: Offset slider in the audio menu. A beat off: tap TAP a few times.
